profile.name: Scott Moss
profile.tagline: AI engineer, building zero-to-one AI products
profile.description: Scott Moss builds zero-to-one AI products and solutions, drawing on work as a two-time Y Combinator founder and at Netflix. He also researches AI safety and shares what he learns.
intro: I take AI products and solutions from zero to one. I’ve built and owned AI architecture and product as a two-time {yc} founder and an engineer at {netflix}, from the first prototype to systems that hold up in production.

As an applied AI architect, I help startups and enterprises do the same, from choosing the right problems to shipping products that work. I also research AI safety: how AI systems fail and how to make them safe. And I create content sharing what I learn.

items.name: Direction
items.description: A Mac app for directors. You give notes in plain language, and an AI editor cuts the film and answers every one. You never touch a timeline.

items.name: Somae
items.description: An inbox for everything your agents make. Agents ask when they need you, you review the real work, from a film to a live site, and your notes go straight back to the agent.

items.title: When everyone is aligned but the system fails
items.premise: Agents that each behave responsibly can still fail as a group: an incident everyone assumes someone else owns, or a warning that never reaches the one agent able to fix it. I’m running a simulated engineering org of 5 to 20 agents to measure how these failures grow with the team, and whether explicit ownership and escalation rules prevent them.

items.title: Safety memory for monitoring long-running agents
items.premise: A safety monitor can miss a violation when the evidence is spread across sessions, tools or agents: one agent reads a secret, another later sends it out, and each step looks harmless on its own. I’m testing whether a compact, persistent record of what matters for safety catches these as well as replaying the full history, at a fraction of the cost.
